info.title: higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-std
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-std", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description:
Real wire request for Higgsfield's Kling 3.0 std/pro/4k text-to-video endpoints. The three tiers share one documented input schema; the tier itself is the PATH segment, so it has no body field here. `prompt` is not required because Higgsfield documents a multi-shot form (`multi_shots: true` with `multi_prompt`) in which the top-level prompt is unused. Comfy Router publishes and ENFORCES this schema for all three tiers: `POST /v2/models/higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-{std,pro,4k}` forwards the body below to Higgsfield untranslated, and a body outside the bounds declared here is refused with `422 invalid_input` before any provider is dialled.
`std` additionally has a SECOND route, which does not take this body: the alternate-provider leg `kling/kling-v3?model_provider=higgsfield` takes `kling/kling-v3`'s own Kling-native body (with `mode`), is validated against that model's authored schema, and is translated onto this wire shape before dispatch. Build a Higgsfield body for `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-std` and a Kling body for `kling/kling-v3?model_provider=higgsfield`; they are not interchangeable.

example.prompt: A cinematic glass pavilion in a misty pine forest at sunrise

cfg_scale.description: How strongly the generation follows the prompt. Higgsfield documents 0-1 in increments of 0.01, but only the 0-1 bound is declared here: a `multipleOf: 0.01` would be evaluated in binary floating point and would refuse ordinary values such as 0.3, so a finer-grained value is ACCEPTED and forwarded rather than refused, the same way `prompt` caveats its undeclared length ceiling.

duration.description: Output duration in seconds. Supported range: 3-15.

elements.description: Reusable Kling element ids, for subject consistency across generations.

multi_prompt.description: Ordered shot definitions, used when `multi_shots` is true. 1-6 shots; the per-shot durations are bounded by the task's own total duration, which is not expressible here.

multi_shots.description: Enable a multi-shot sequence. When true, `multi_prompt` carries the per-shot definitions.

prompt.description: Prompt describing the desired output. Higgsfield documents that Kling uses up to the first 2,500 characters and truncates beyond that, so no maxLength is declared — a longer body is accepted, not refused.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Higgsfield's request envelope, returned BOTH by a generation POST (as `{status: "queued", request_id, status_url, cancel_url}`) and by the shared status route, which adds the output once the request completes. Only the video output is modelled here because the two enrolled families are video models; Higgsfield's own shared component also carries image and audio outputs for families Comfy does not enrol.
This is also the Comfy Router output schema for every Higgsfield video id Router publishes — `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-{std,pro,4k}`, `higgsfield/higgsfield-kling-3-turbo` and `higgsfield/higgsfield-wan-3`. All five are SUBMIT-AND-POLL: Router polls the shared status route on the caller's behalf, so the body a caller receives is this TERMINAL document rather than the queued handle the generation POST answers with. A caller therefore reads `status: "completed"` with the download URL at `video.url`; `queued` and `in_progress` are in-flight states Router does not return, and `nsfw`, `failed` and `canceled` are the terminal failures. `url` is required on the video output, so a `completed` carrying no `video` is a contract break rather than a finished generation.

cancel_url.description: Absolute URL used to cancel a request before processing starts.

request_id.description: Stable identifier used for polling, cancellation and support.

status_url.description: Absolute URL to poll until the request reaches a terminal state.

HiggsfieldKling30Shot.description: One shot of a Higgsfield Kling 3.0 multi-shot sequence.

duration.description: Duration of this shot in seconds, 1-15. The sum across shots must not exceed the task's total duration, which JSON Schema cannot express; Higgsfield enforces it.

prompt.description: Prompt for this shot. Higgsfield documents a 512-character ceiling.

url.description: Download URL of the generated media.
